663: func fingerprintOperationInputs(root, canonical string, inputs []string) (string, error) {
664: 	hash := sha256.New()
665: 	_, _ = hash.Write([]byte(canonical))
666: 	for _, rel := range inputs {
667: 		path := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
668: 		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
669: 		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
670: 			continue
671: 		}
672: 		if err != nil {
673: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect governed input %s: %w", rel, err)
674: 		}
675: 		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
676: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("governed input %s must not be a symbolic link", rel)
677: 		}
678: 		if info.IsDir() {
679: 			var files []string
680: 			if err := filepath.WalkDir(path, func(item string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
681: 				if walkErr != nil {
682: 					return walkErr
683: 				}
684: 				if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
685: 					return fmt.Errorf("governed input %s must not contain symbolic links", rel)
686: 				}
687: 				if !entry.IsDir() {
688: 					files = append(files, item)
689: 				}
690: 				return nil
691: 			}); err != nil {
692: 				return "", fmt.Errorf("scan governed input %s: %w", rel, err)
693: 			}
694: 			sort.Strings(files)
695: 			for _, item := range files {
696: 				itemRel, _ := filepath.Rel(root, item)
697: 				if err := hashOperationFile(hash, item, filepath.ToSlash(itemRel)); err != nil {
698: 					return "", err
699: 				}
700: 			}
701: 			continue
702: 		}
703: 		if err := hashOperationFile(hash, path, rel); err != nil {
704: 			return "", err
705: 		}
706: 	}
707: 	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
708: }

710: func hashOperationFile(hash interface{ Write([]byte) (int, error) }, path, rel string) error {
711: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)

714: 	}
715: 	_, _ = hash.Write([]byte("\x00" + rel + "\x00"))
716: 	_, _ = hash.Write(data)
717: 	return nil
718: }

752: 	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
753: 		r.State = OperationCancelled
754: 	} else {
755: 		r.State = OperationFailed
756: 	}
757: 	cause := displaySafe(err.Error())
758: 	code, category, guidance := "internal.error", "internal", "Inspect durable state and retry after correcting the reported cause."
759: 	if smokeErr, ok := sprint.AsSmokeError(err); ok {
760: 		code, category, guidance = smokeErr.Code, smokeErr.Category, smokeErr.Guidance
761: 		r.Message = operationFailureMessage(category)
762: 		r.Error = &OperationError{Code: code, Category: category, Operation: "smoke", Component: "sprint", Message: r.Message, Cause: cause, Guidance: guidance, Retryable: category == "process" || category == "timeout"}
763: 		return r, err
764: 	}
765: 	if qaErr, ok := sprint.AsQAError(err); ok {
766: 		category = string(qaErr.Category)
767: 		code = "qa." + category
768: 		guidance = qaErr.Recovery
769: 		switch qaErr.Category {
770: 		case sprint.QAErrorRuntimeUnavailable, sprint.QAErrorPersistenceFailure:
771: 			category = "runtime"
772: 		case sprint.QAErrorConflict:
773: 			category = "concurrency"
774: 		default:
775: 			category = "validation"
776: 		}
777: 		r.Message = operationFailureMessage(category)
778: 		r.Error = &OperationError{Code: code, Category: category, Operation: "qa", Component: "sprint", Message: r.Message, Cause: cause, Guidance: guidance, Retryable: qaErr.Category == sprint.QAErrorRuntimeUnavailable || qaErr.Category == sprint.QAErrorConflict}
779: 		return r, err
780: 	}
781: 	var projectRef project.RefError
782: 	var sprintRef sprint.RefError
783: 	switch {
784: 	case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
785: 		code, category, guidance = "workflow.cancelled", "cancellation", "Resume the operation when ready."
786: 	case errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrFlowStateMalformed), errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrFlowStateUnsupported),
787: 		errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrExecuteRunStateMissing), errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed), errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrExecuteRunStateUnsupported),
788: 		errors.As(err, &projectRef), errors.As(err, &sprintRef), len(r.Findings) > 0:
789: 		code, category, guidance = "validation.reference", "validation", "Complete or repair the reported governed evidence, inspect validation findings, and retry."
790: 	case errors.Is(err, sprint.ErrVerificationConflict), errors.Is(err, ErrStaleOperation):
791: 		code, category, guidance = "workflow.locked", "concurrency", "Inspect the active or stale study lock before retrying."
792: 	}
793: 	r.Message = operationFailureMessage(category)
794: 	r.Error = &OperationError{Code: code, Category: category, Operation: "workflow.operation", Component: "app", Message: r.Message, Cause: cause, Guidance: guidance, Retryable: category == "runtime" || category == "concurrency"}
795: 	return r, err
796: }

875: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
876: 		return ValidationOperationResult{}, err
877: 	}
878: 	result := ValidationOperationResult{Operation: "validate", Status: "valid"}
879: 	switch req.Subject {
880: 	case ValidationProject:
881: 		ref := strings.TrimSpace(req.Project)
882: 		validation, err := project.NewService(u.root).Validate(ref)
883: 		if err != nil {
884: 			return result, mapProjectError("project.validate", err)
885: 		}
886: 		result.Subject = ref
887: 		result.Status = string(validation.Status)
888: 		for _, finding := range validation.Findings {
889: 			result.Findings = append(result.Findings, projectFinding(finding))
890: 		}
891: 	case ValidationStudy:
892: 		ref := strings.TrimSpace(req.Study)
893: 		validation, err := study.NewService(u.root).ValidateStudy(ref)
894: 		if err != nil {
895: 			return result, mapStudyError(err)
896: 		}
897: 		result.Subject = ref
898: 		result.Status = string(validation.Status)
899: 		for _, check := range validation.Checks {
900: 			if check.Status != study.ValidationStatusPassed {
901: 				result.Findings = append(result.Findings, studyFinding(check))
902: 			}
903: 		}
904: 		for _, report := range validation.Reports {
905: 			for _, check := range report.Checks {
906: 				if check.Status != study.ValidationStatusPassed {
907: 					result.Findings = append(result.Findings, studyFinding(check))
908: 				}
909: 			}
910: 		}
911: 	case ValidationSprint:
912: 		stage := sprint.PlanningStage(strings.TrimSpace(req.Stage))
913: 		validation, err := validateSprintStage(u.sprintService(), req.Project, req.Sprint, stage)
914: 		if err != nil {
915: 			return result, mapSprintError("sprint.validate", err)
916: 		}
917: 		result.Subject = strings.TrimSpace(req.Project) + "/" + strings.TrimSpace(req.Sprint) + "/" + string(stage)
918: 		if !validation.Valid() {
919: 			result.Status = "invalid"
920: 		}
921: 		for _, finding := range validation.Findings {
922: 			result.Findings = append(result.Findings, sprintFinding(finding))
923: 		}
924: 	default:
925: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("validate: unsupported subject %q", req.Subject)
926: 	}
927: 	sort.SliceStable(result.Findings, func(i, j int) bool {
928: 		a, b := result.Findings[i], result.Findings[j]
929: 		if a.Path != b.Path {
930: 			return a.Path < b.Path
931: 		}
932: 		if a.Section != b.Section {
933: 			return a.Section < b.Section
934: 		}
935: 		return a.Problem < b.Problem
936: 	})
937: 	return result, nil
938: }

220: 	if err := validateQAOperationRequest(req); err != nil {
221: 		return Confirmation{}, err
222: 	}
223: 	if (req.Kind == OperationReviewStart || req.Kind == OperationReviewDryRun) && req.Parallelism <= 0 {
224: 		req.Parallelism = u.reviewConcurrency
225: 	}
226: 	c := Confirmation{Request: req, Subject: operationFirstNonEmpty(req.Project+"/"+req.Sprint, req.Study), Permission: "workspace policy enforced"}
227: 	switch req.Kind {
228: 	case OperationValidate, OperationPrompt, OperationFlowDryRun, OperationStageDryRun, OperationExecuteDryRun, OperationExecuteStatus, OperationReviewDryRun, OperationReviewStatus, OperationSmokeStatus, OperationQAStatus:
229: 		c.Scope = []string{req.Stage}
230: 		c.Warning = "runtime-free; no runtime-backed writes"
231: 	case OperationQADryRun:
232: 		mapped, err := u.QAMap(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
233: 		if err != nil {
234: 			return c, err
235: 		}
236: 		c.Scope = []string{fmt.Sprintf("deterministic map %s", mapped.MapFingerprint), fmt.Sprintf("%d changed paths in %d bounded shards", mapped.ChangedPaths, mapped.TotalShards)}
237: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME-FREE; TARGET AND GOVERNED INPUTS READ-ONLY; NO QA STATE WRITE"
238: 	case OperationQAStart, OperationQAResume:
239: 		mapped, err := u.QAMap(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
240: 		if err != nil {
241: 			return c, err
242: 		}
243: 		if req.Task != "" {
244: 			owned := false
245: 			for _, shard := range mapped.Shards {
246: 				owned = owned || shard.ID == req.Task
247: 			}
248: 			if !owned {
249: 				return c, fmt.Errorf("selected QA shard is not owned by the current map")
250: 			}
251: 		}
252: 		c.Runtime, c.Mutates = true, true
253: 		c.Scope = []string{fmt.Sprintf("deterministic map %s", mapped.MapFingerprint), fmt.Sprintf("bounded concurrency and %d total shards", mapped.TotalShards)}
254: 		if req.Task != "" {
255: 			c.Scope = append(c.Scope, "map-owned shard "+req.Task)
256: 		}
257: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + PRIVATE QA STATE WRITE; IMPLEMENTATION TARGET READ-ONLY"
258: 	case OperationQARecover:
259: 		c.Mutates = true
260: 		c.Scope = []string{"QA pointer, digest, interrupted ownership, flow summary, and retention reconciliation"}
261: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME-FREE QA RECOVERY; NO CHILD WORK"
262: 	case OperationSprintStatus:
263: 		c.Mutates = true
264: 		c.Scope = []string{"all sprint stages", "execute and Conformance Review state"}
265: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME-FREE; MAY REFRESH FLOW-STATE.JSON"
266: 	case OperationFlow:
267: 		c.Runtime = true
268: 		c.Mutates = true
269: 		c.Scope = []string{"planning stages through " + req.Stage}
270: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + WORKSPACE MUTATION"
271: 	case OperationStage:
272: 		c.Runtime = true
273: 		c.Mutates = true
274: 		c.Scope = []string{"selected planning stage only: " + req.Stage}
275: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + WORKSPACE MUTATION; PREREQUISITES MUST ALREADY BE VALID"
276: 	case OperationExecuteStart, OperationExecuteResume:
277: 		c.Runtime = true
278: 		c.Mutates = true
279: 		c.Scope = []string{"execute tasks"}
280: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + APPROVED TARGET MUTATION"
281: 	case OperationReviewStart:
282: 		c.Runtime = true
283: 		c.Mutates = true
284: 		c.Scope = []string{"one read-only Conformance Review worker per selected contract plus handbook", fmt.Sprintf("bounded parallelism: %d", req.Parallelism)}
285: 		if req.RestartReview {
286: 			c.Scope = append(c.Scope, "discard resumable Conformance Review checkpoints and start fresh sessions")
287: 		}
288: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + REVIEW ARTIFACT WRITE (TARGET READ-ONLY)"
289: 	case OperationSmokeDryRun, OperationSmokeStart:
290: 		preview, err := u.sprintService().RunSmoke(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.SmokeRequest{Level: req.Level, Suite: req.Suite, Test: req.Test, ForceReview: req.ForceReview, OverrideConfirmed: req.ForceReview, OverrideRationale: req.OverrideRationale, DryRun: true})
291: 		if err != nil {
292: 			return c, err
293: 		}
294: 		c.Runtime = true
295: 		c.Mutates = req.Kind == OperationSmokeStart
296: 		c.Scope = []string{fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", preview.ScopeKind, preview.Scope), preview.ScopeRationale, "prerequisites: " + strings.Join(preview.Prerequisites, ", "), "duration/cost: " + preview.DurationClass + "/" + preview.CostClass, fmt.Sprintf("timeout: %s (source: %s)", preview.EffectiveTimeout, preview.TimeoutSource), "safe command: " + preview.SafeArgv, "evidence roots: " + strings.Join(preview.EvidenceRoots, ", ")}
297: 		c.Warning = "EXTERNAL HARNESS + SMOKE ARTIFACT WRITE; RAW EVIDENCE REMAINS EXTERNAL"
298: 	case OperationVerifyDryRun, OperationVerifyStart:
299: 		c.Runtime, c.Mutates = true, req.Kind == OperationVerifyStart
300: 		c.Scope = []string{"complete execute evidence", "current Conformance Review", "Conformance Review-gated containing smoke scope"}
301: 		if req.ForceReview {
302: 			c.Scope = append(c.Scope, "DIAGNOSTIC OVERRIDE: "+req.OverrideRationale)
303: 		}
304: 		c.Warning = "ORDERED REVIEW -> SMOKE VERIFICATION; CANONICAL EVIDENCE ONLY AFTER VALIDATION"
305: 	case OperationStudyStart, OperationStudyResume:
306: 		if req.Parallelism < 1 || req.Parallelism > 64 {
307: 			return c, fmt.Errorf("parallelism must be between 1 and 64")
308: 		}
309: 		c.Runtime = true
310: 		c.Mutates = true
311: 		c.Scope = []string{fmt.Sprintf("study run-loop with %d parallel workers", req.Parallelism)}
312: 		c.Warning = "RUNTIME + STUDY STATE MUTATION"
313: 	case OperationStudyCancel:
314: 		c.Mutates = true
315: 		c.Scope = []string{"active study run-loop"}
316: 		c.Warning = "CANCEL ACTIVE RUN LOOP"
317: 	default:
318: 		return c, fmt.Errorf("unsupported operation %q", req.Kind)
319: 	}
320: 	if req.Project != "" {
321: 		if req.Sprint != "" {
322: 			c.Paths = []string{"projects/" + req.Project + "/sprints/" + req.Sprint}
323: 			c.DurableRefreshPath = "/api/v1/projects/" + req.Project + "/sprints/" + req.Sprint
324: 		} else {
325: 			c.Paths = []string{"projects/" + req.Project}
326: 			c.DurableRefreshPath = "/api/v1/projects/" + req.Project
327: 		}
328: 	} else {
329: 		c.Paths = []string{"studies/" + req.Study}
330: 		c.DurableRefreshPath = "/api/v1/studies/" + req.Study
331: 	}
332: 	if c.Mutates {
333: 		if req.Project != "" {
334: 			c.MutationClass = "sprint_mutation"
335: 		} else {
336: 			c.MutationClass = "study_mutation"
337: 		}
338: 	} else {
339: 		c.MutationClass = "read_only"
340: 	}
341: 	if c.Runtime {
342: 		c.ModelSource = operationRuntimeIdentity(req, u.stageRuntime)
343: 	}
344: 	c.Prerequisites = operationPrerequisites(req)
345: 	canonical, err := canonicalOperationRequest(req)
346: 	if err != nil {
347: 		return c, err
348: 	}
349: 	c.CanonicalRequest = canonical
350: 	c.GovernedInputs = governedOperationInputs(req)
351: 	fingerprintBasis := canonical + "\nruntime=" + c.ModelSource + "\nscope=" + strings.Join(c.Scope, "\x00")
352: 	fingerprint, err := fingerprintOperationInputs(u.root, fingerprintBasis, c.GovernedInputs)
353: 	if err != nil {
354: 		return c, err
355: 	}
356: 	c.InputFingerprint = fingerprint
357: 	c.Request.ExpectedFingerprint = fingerprint
358: 	return c, nil
359: }

361: func validateQAOperationRequest(req OperationRequest) error {
362: 	switch req.Kind {
363: 	case OperationQAStatus, OperationQADryRun, OperationQAStart, OperationQAResume, OperationQARecover:
364: 	default:
365: 		return nil
366: 	}
367: 	if req.Study != "" || req.Stage != "" || req.Model != "" || req.Level != "" || req.Suite != "" || req.Test != "" || req.Timeout != "" || req.ForceReview || req.RestartReview || req.OverrideRationale != "" || len(req.ReviewFocus) > 0 || len(req.Sources) > 0 || len(req.Dimensions) > 0 || req.Parallelism != 0 {
368: 		return fmt.Errorf("QA operations accept only project, sprint, and a map-owned shard")
369: 	}
370: 	if req.Task != "" && req.Kind != OperationQAStart && req.Kind != OperationQAResume {
371: 		return fmt.Errorf("QA shard is valid only for start or resume")
372: 	}
373: 	return nil
374: }

376: func (u dashboardUseCases) RunOperation(ctx context.Context, req OperationRequest, emit func(OperationEvent)) (OperationResult, error) {
377: 	expected := req.ExpectedFingerprint
378: 	req.ExpectedFingerprint = ""
379: 	prepared, err := u.PrepareOperation(ctx, req)
380: 	if err != nil {
381: 		return failedOperation(OperationResult{Subject: operationFirstNonEmpty(req.Project+"/"+req.Sprint, req.Study)}, err)
382: 	}
383: 	if expected != "" && expected != prepared.InputFingerprint {
384: 		return failedOperation(OperationResult{Subject: prepared.Subject}, ErrStaleOperation)
385: 	}
386: 	req = prepared.Request
387: 	if emit == nil {
388: 		emit = func(OperationEvent) {}
389: 	}
390: 	emit(OperationEvent{State: OperationRunning, Stage: req.Stage, Message: "operation started"})
391: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
392: 		return OperationResult{State: OperationCancelled}, err
393: 	}
394: 	ss := u.sprintService()
395: 	result := OperationResult{State: OperationComplete, Subject: operationFirstNonEmpty(req.Project+"/"+req.Sprint, req.Study)}
396: 	stage := sprint.PlanningStage(req.Stage)
397: 	switch req.Kind {
398: 	case OperationValidate:
399: 		validationReq := ValidationRequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint, Study: req.Study, Stage: req.Stage}
400: 		switch {
401: 		case req.Study != "":
402: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationStudy
403: 		case req.Sprint != "":
404: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationSprint
405: 		default:
406: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationProject
407: 		}
408: 		validation, err := u.Validate(ctx, validationReq)
409: 		if err != nil {
410: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
411: 		}
412: 		result.Message = validation.Status
413: 		result.Findings = append(result.Findings, validation.Findings...)
414: 	case OperationSprintStatus:
415: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
416: 		if err != nil {
417: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
418: 		}
419: 		result.Message = summarizeSprintStatus(r)
420: 	case OperationPrompt:
421: 		p, err := promptSprintStage(ss, req.Project, req.Sprint, stage)
422: 		if err != nil {
423: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
424: 		}
425: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(p.Prompt)
426: 	case OperationFlowDryRun:
427: 		r, err := runSprintFlow(ctx, ss, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.FlowRequest{To: stage, DryRun: true})
428: 		if err != nil {
429: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
430: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
431: 		}
432: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Message)
433: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("flow to %s dry run", stage)
434: 	case OperationStageDryRun:
435: 		r, err := ss.FlowStage(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.FlowRequest{To: stage, DryRun: true})
436: 		if err != nil {
437: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
438: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
439: 		}
440: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Message)
441: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("single-stage %s dry run", stage)
442: 	case OperationExecuteDryRun:
443: 		r, err := ss.Execute(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.ExecuteRequest{DryRun: true, TaskID: req.Task})
444: 		if err != nil {
445: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
446: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
447: 		}
448: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Prompt)
449: 		result.Message = r.Message
450: 	case OperationExecuteStatus:
451: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
452: 		if err != nil {
453: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
454: 		}
455: 		execute := summarizeExecute(r.ExecuteState)
456: 		if !execute.Available {
457: 			result.Message = execute.Message
458: 		} else {
459: 			result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%d total: %d pending, %d running, %d complete, %d failed, %d cancelled", execute.Total, execute.Pending, execute.Running, execute.Complete, execute.Failed, execute.Cancelled)
460: 		}
461: 	case OperationReviewDryRun:
462: 		r, err := ss.Review(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.ReviewRequest{DryRun: true, Concurrency: req.Parallelism})
463: 		if err != nil {
464: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
465: 		}
466: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Prompt)
467: 		result.Message = r.Message
468: 	case OperationReviewStatus:
469: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
470: 		if err != nil {
471: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
472: 		}
473: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s verdict=%s fresh=%t next=%s", r.Verification.Review.ExecutionStatus, r.Verification.Review.Verdict, r.Verification.Review.Fresh, r.Verification.Review.NextAction)
474: 	case OperationSmokeStatus:
475: 		r, err := ss.VerificationStatus(req.Project, req.Sprint)
476: 		if err != nil {
477: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
478: 		}
479: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s verdict=%s fresh=%t run=%s issues=%d assessment=%s next=%s", r.Smoke.ExecutionStatus, r.Smoke.Verdict, r.Smoke.Fresh, r.Smoke.RunID, len(r.Smoke.Issues), r.Assessment, r.NextAction)
480: 	case OperationSmokeDryRun:
481: 		r, err := ss.RunSmoke(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.SmokeRequest{Level: req.Level, Suite: req.Suite, Test: req.Test, ForceReview: req.ForceReview, OverrideConfirmed: req.ForceReview, OverrideRationale: req.OverrideRationale, DryRun: true})
482: 		if err != nil {
483: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
484: 		}
485: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %s", r.ScopeKind, r.Scope, r.ScopeRationale)
486: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(sprint.RenderSmoke(r))
487: 	case OperationQAStatus:
488: 		qa, err := u.QAStatus(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
489: 		if err != nil {
490: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
491: 		}
492: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("phase=%s fresh=%t shards=%d/%d next=%s", qa.Phase, qa.Fresh, qa.CompletedShards, qa.TotalShards, qa.NextAction)
493: 	case OperationQADryRun:
494: 		qa, err := u.QAMap(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
495: 		if err != nil {
496: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
497: 		}
498: 		data, _ := json.MarshalIndent(qa, "", "  ")
499: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(string(data))
500: 		result.Message = "read-only QA map ready"
501: 	case OperationQARecover:
502: 		qa, err := u.RecoverQA(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
503: 		if err != nil {
504: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
505: 		}
506: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("phase=%s next=%s", qa.Phase, qa.NextAction)
507: 	case OperationVerifyDryRun:
508: 		r, err := ss.Verify(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.VerifyRequest{To: sprint.PlanningStage(req.Stage), DryRun: true, Review: sprint.ReviewRequest{DryRun: true, Focus: req.ReviewFocus, Restart: req.RestartReview}, Smoke: sprint.SmokeRequest{Level: req.Level, Suite: req.Suite, Test: req.Test, ForceReview: req.ForceReview, OverrideConfirmed: req.ForceReview, OverrideRationale: req.OverrideRationale, DryRun: true}})
509: 		if err != nil {
510: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
511: 		}
512: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("assessment=%s next=%s", r.Verification.Assessment, r.Verification.NextAction)
513: 	default:
514: 		if u.runner == nil {
515: 			return failedOperation(result, fmt.Errorf("runtime-backed operation is unavailable without configured composition"))
516: 		}
517: 		return u.runner(ctx, req, emit)
518: 	}
519: 	emit(OperationEvent{State: OperationComplete, Stage: req.Stage, Message: operationFirstNonEmpty(result.Message, "operation complete")})
520: 	return result, nil
521: }

541: func validateOperationScope(req OperationRequest) error {
542: 	for name, value := range map[string]string{"project": req.Project, "sprint": req.Sprint, "study": req.Study} {
543: 		if value == "" {
544: 			continue
545: 		}
546: 		if value == "." || value == ".." || len(value) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(value, `/\\`) {
547: 			return fmt.Errorf("invalid operation %s reference", name)
548: 		}
549: 		for _, r := range value {
550: 			if (r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || r == '.' || r == '_' || r == '-' {
551: 				continue
552: 			}
553: 			return fmt.Errorf("invalid operation %s reference", name)
554: 		}
555: 	}
556: 	return nil
557: }

559: func normalizedStrings(values []string) []string {
560: 	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
561: 	out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
562: 	for _, value := range values {
563: 		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
564: 		if value == "" {
565: 			continue
566: 		}
567: 		if _, ok := seen[value]; ok {
568: 			continue
569: 		}
570: 		seen[value] = struct{}{}
571: 		out = append(out, value)
572: 	}
573: 	sort.Strings(out)
574: 	return out
575: }

603: func operationRuntimeIdentity(req OperationRequest, stages map[sprint.PlanningStage]sprint.StageRuntime) string {
604: 	if req.Model != "" {
605: 		return "requested model " + req.Model
606: 	}
607: 	stage := sprint.PlanningStage(req.Stage)
608: 	switch req.Kind {
609: 	case OperationExecuteStart, OperationExecuteResume:
610: 		stage = sprint.StageExecute
611: 	case OperationReviewStart:
612: 		stage = sprint.StageReview
613: 	case OperationSmokeStart, OperationVerifyStart:
614: 		stage = sprint.StageSmoke
615: 	case OperationQAStart, OperationQAResume:
616: 		return "configured QA runtime"
617: 	}
618: 	if runtime, ok := stages[stage]; ok && (runtime.Model != "" || runtime.Variant != "") {
619: 		return strings.TrimSpace(runtime.Model + " variant=" + runtime.Variant)
620: 	}
621: 	if req.Kind == OperationSmokeStart {
622: 		return "configured smoke author and harness"
623: 	}
624: 	return "effective workspace runtime configuration"
625: }

158: func (m *durableOperationManager) RecordOperationEvent(ctx context.Context, runID string, event OperationEvent) (bool, error) {

229: 		select {
230: 		case <-ctx.Done():

232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return
234: 		case now := <-ticker.C:
235: 			snapshot, err := m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, owned.fence.RunID)
236: 			if err != nil {

238: 				return
239: 			}

241: 				if _, _, err := m.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx, owned.fence); err != nil {

243: 					return

246: 				return

249: 				if _, err := m.repository.Heartbeat(ctx, owned.fence, runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration); err != nil {

251: 					return
252: 				}

257: 					owned.cancel()
258: 					return

261: 			}
262: 		}

34: // durableCLICommand is the synchronous CLI counterpart to the web/TUI
35: // acceptance boundary. It keeps the manager alive for the whole command and
36: // gives product code the cancellation-aware context owned by the durable run.
37: type durableCLICommand struct {
38: 	manager  *durableOperationManager
39: 	accepted AcceptedOperation
40: }

45: 	repository runcontrol.Repository
46: 	fence      runcontrol.Fence

49: func beginDurableCLICommand(deps dependencies, request OperationRequest) (*durableCLICommand, error) {
50: 	repository, _, err := runRepository(deps)
51: 	if err != nil {
52: 		return nil, err
53: 	}
54: 	manager := newDurableOperationManager(repository, deps.runControl.owner)
55: 	accepted, err := manager.AcceptOperation(deps.ctx, Confirmation{Request: request}, "")
56: 	if err != nil {
57: 		return nil, classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, err, "run-control.accept")
58: 	}
59: 	return &durableCLICommand{manager: manager, accepted: accepted}, nil
60: }

62: func (c *durableCLICommand) Context() context.Context { return c.accepted.Context }

64: func (c *durableCLICommand) QAWriterToken() (sprint.QAWriterToken, func(sprint.QAWriterToken) error, error) {
65: 	if c == nil {
66: 		return sprint.QAWriterToken{}, nil, errors.New("durable QA ownership is unavailable")
67: 	}
68: 	return qaOwnershipFromContext(c.accepted.Context)
69: }

71: func (c *durableCLICommand) Finish(runErr error) error {
72: 	state := OperationComplete
73: 	if c.accepted.Context.Err() != nil {
74: 		state = OperationCancelled
75: 	} else if runErr != nil {
76: 		state = OperationFailed
77: 	}
78: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
79: 	defer cancel()
80: 	if err := c.manager.FinishOperation(ctx, c.accepted.RunID, state, runErr); err != nil {
81: 		return classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, err, "run-control.finish")
82: 	}
83: 	return nil
84: }

86: func finishDurableCLICommand(command *durableCLICommand, runErr error) error {
87: 	if command == nil {
88: 		return runErr
89: 	}
90: 	return errors.Join(runErr, command.Finish(runErr))
91: }

93: func newDurableOperationManager(repository runcontrol.Repository, owner runcontrol.Owner) *durableOperationManager {
94: 	return &durableOperationManager{repository: repository, owner: owner, owned: make(map[string]*ownedDurableOperation)}
95: }
96: 
97: func (m *durableOperationManager) AcceptOperation(ctx context.Context, confirmation Confirmation, digest string) (AcceptedOperation, error) {
98: 	req := confirmation.Request
99: 	target := runcontrol.Target{
100: 		Kind: "operation", Operation: string(req.Kind), Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint,
101: 		Study: req.Study, Stage: req.Stage, Task: req.Task,
102: 	}
103: 	snapshot, err := m.repository.Accept(ctx, runcontrol.Acceptance{
104: 		Target: target, ProductStatus: "prepared", OperationAlias: digest, ConfirmationDigest: digest,
105: 	})
106: 	if err != nil && digest != "" && errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrConflict) {
107: 		existing, resolveErr := m.repository.ResolveOperationAlias(ctx, digest)
108: 		if resolveErr != nil {
109: 			return AcceptedOperation{}, errors.Join(err, resolveErr)
110: 		}
111: 		return AcceptedOperation{RunID: string(existing.RunID), Context: ctx, Existing: true, Lifecycle: string(existing.Lifecycle)}, nil
112: 	}
113: 	if err != nil {
114: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation acceptance: %w", err)
115: 	}
116: 	attempt, _, err := m.repository.Claim(ctx, runcontrol.Claim{RunID: snapshot.RunID, Owner: m.owner, Lease: runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration})
117: 	if err != nil {
118: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation owner claim: %w", err)
119: 	}
120: 	fence := runcontrol.Fence{RunID: snapshot.RunID, AttemptID: attempt.ID, OwnerID: m.owner.ID, FencingGeneration: attempt.FencingGeneration}
121: 	if _, _, err := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
122: 		Type: runcontrol.EventLifecycle, Lifecycle: runcontrol.LifecycleRunning,
123: 		Payload: map[string]string{"lifecycle": string(runcontrol.LifecycleRunning)},
124: 	}); err != nil {
125: 		terminalCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
126: 		_, _, _ = proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, m.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{Outcome: runcontrol.TerminalPersistenceLost, Reason: "operation start persistence failed", ProposedBy: m.owner.ID})
127: 		cancel()
128: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation start: %w", err)
129: 	}
130: 	operationCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(runcontrol.WithParentRun(ctx, snapshot.RunID))
131: 	operationCtx = context.WithValue(operationCtx, durableOperationContextKey{}, durableOperationOwnership{repository: m.repository, fence: fence})
132: 	owned := &ownedDurableOperation{fence: fence, cancel: cancel, stop: make(chan struct{}), done: make(chan struct{})}
133: 	m.mu.Lock()
134: 	m.owned[string(snapshot.RunID)] = owned
135: 	m.mu.Unlock()
136: 	go m.controlOperation(operationCtx, owned)
137: 	return AcceptedOperation{RunID: string(snapshot.RunID), Context: operationCtx, Lifecycle: string(runcontrol.LifecycleRunning)}, nil
138: }
139: 
140: func qaOwnershipFromContext(ctx context.Context) (sprint.QAWriterToken, func(sprint.QAWriterToken) error, error) {
141: 	ownership, ok := ctx.Value(durableOperationContextKey{}).(durableOperationOwnership)
142: 	if !ok || ownership.repository == nil {
143: 		return sprint.QAWriterToken{}, nil, errors.New("durable QA ownership is missing from the operation context")
144: 	}
145: 	token := sprint.QAWriterToken{RunID: string(ownership.fence.RunID), OperationalAttemptID: string(ownership.fence.AttemptID), FencingGeneration: ownership.fence.FencingGeneration}
146: 	fence := func(got sprint.QAWriterToken) error {
147: 		if got != token {
148: 			return runcontrol.ErrStaleFence
149: 		}
150: 		fenceCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
151: 		defer cancel()
152: 		_, err := ownership.repository.Heartbeat(fenceCtx, ownership.fence, runControlLease)
153: 		return err
154: 	}
155: 	return token, fence, nil
156: }
157: 
158: func (m *durableOperationManager) RecordOperationEvent(ctx context.Context, runID string, event OperationEvent) (bool, error) {
159: 	m.mu.Lock()
160: 	owned := m.owned[runID]
161: 	m.mu.Unlock()
162: 	if owned == nil {
163: 		return false, runcontrol.ErrNotFound
164: 	}
165: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
166: 	defer owned.eventMu.Unlock()
167: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
168: 	if event.State == OperationFailed {
169: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
170: 	}
171: 	key := string(eventType) + "\x00" + event.Stage + "\x00" + event.Task + "\x00" + event.PhaseState + "\x00" + event.SafeSummary + "\x00" + event.EventType + "\x00" + event.EventKind + "\x00" + event.Tool + "\x00" + event.Reason + "\x00" + event.Detail
172: 	now := time.Now().UTC()
173: 	elapsed := now.Sub(owned.progressAt)
174: 	if eventType == runcontrol.EventProgress && key == owned.progressKey && elapsed >= 0 && elapsed < runcontrol.ProgressCoalesceWindow {
175: 		if owned.omitted == 0 {
176: 			owned.omittedFirst = now
177: 		}
178: 		owned.omitted++
179: 		owned.omittedLast = now
180: 		return false, nil
181: 	}
182: 	payload := map[string]string{
183: 		"state": string(event.State), "type": event.EventType,
184: 		"count": fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", event.Completed, event.Total),
185: 	}
186: 	for key, value := range map[string]string{
187: 		"phase_state": event.PhaseState, "summary": event.SafeSummary,
188: 		"tool_call_id": event.ToolCallID, "tool_status": event.ToolStatus,
189: 		"tool_arguments": event.ToolArguments, "tool_result": event.ToolResult, "tool_error": event.ToolError,
190: 		"provider": event.Provider, "model": event.Model, "harness": event.Harness,
191: 	} {
192: 		if value != "" {
193: 			payload[key] = value
194: 		}
195: 	}
196: 	var omission *runcontrol.Omission
197: 	if event.Message != "" {
198: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "presentation message omitted", Count: 1}
199: 	}
200: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
201: 		if omission == nil {
202: 			omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}
203: 		}
204: 		omission.Count += owned.omitted
205: 		omission.FirstAt, omission.LastAt = &owned.omittedFirst, &owned.omittedLast
206: 		owned.omitted = 0
207: 	}
208: 	_, _, err := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
209: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeOperation, Stage: event.Stage, Task: event.Task,
210: 		Kind: event.EventKind, Tool: event.Tool, Action: event.Action, Reason: event.Reason,
211: 		Detail: event.Detail, Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
212: 	})
213: 	if err != nil {
214: 		owned.cancel()
215: 		return false, err
216: 	}
217: 	if eventType == runcontrol.EventProgress {
218: 		owned.progressKey, owned.progressAt = key, now
219: 	}
220: 	return true, nil
221: }

223: func (m *durableOperationManager) controlOperation(ctx context.Context, owned *ownedDurableOperation) {
224: 	defer close(owned.done)
225: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
226: 	defer ticker.Stop()
227: 	lastHeartbeat, lastReconcile := time.Now(), time.Now()
228: 	for {
229: 		select {
230: 		case <-ctx.Done():
231: 			return
232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return
234: 		case now := <-ticker.C:
235: 			snapshot, err := m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, owned.fence.RunID)
236: 			if err != nil {
237: 				owned.cancel()
238: 				return
239: 			}
240: 			if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
241: 				if _, _, err := m.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx, owned.fence); err != nil {
242: 					owned.cancel()
243: 					return
244: 				}
245: 				owned.cancel()
246: 				return
247: 			}
248: 			if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
249: 				if _, err := m.repository.Heartbeat(ctx, owned.fence, runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration); err != nil {
250: 					owned.cancel()
251: 					return
252: 				}
253: 				lastHeartbeat = now
254: 			}
255: 			if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
256: 				if _, err := m.repository.Reconcile(ctx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
257: 					owned.cancel()
258: 					return
259: 				}
260: 				lastReconcile = now
261: 			}
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: }
265: 
266: func (m *durableOperationManager) FinishOperation(ctx context.Context, runID string, state OperationState, runErr error) error {
267: 	m.mu.Lock()
268: 	owned := m.owned[runID]
269: 	delete(m.owned, runID)
270: 	m.mu.Unlock()
271: 	if owned == nil {
272: 		return nil
273: 	}
274: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
275: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
276: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{Type: runcontrol.EventOmission, Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: owned.omitted, FirstAt: &owned.omittedFirst, LastAt: &owned.omittedLast}})
277: 		if appendErr != nil && runErr == nil {
278: 			runErr = appendErr
279: 		}
280: 		owned.omitted = 0
281: 	}
282: 	owned.eventMu.Unlock()
283: 	close(owned.stop)
284: 	<-owned.done
285: 	owned.cancel()
286: 	outcome := runcontrol.TerminalSucceeded
287: 	reason := "operation completed"
288: 	switch {
289: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.DeadlineExceeded):
290: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalTimedOut, "operation deadline exceeded"
291: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled), state == OperationCancelled:
292: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalCancelled, "operation cancelled"
293: 	case runErr != nil, state == OperationFailed:
294: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalFailed, "operation failed"
295: 	case state == OperationPartial:
296: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalInterrupted, "operation interrupted"
297: 	}
298: 	_, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: m.owner.ID})
299: 	return err
300: }

# Sprint Requirements: Guarded Web Operations and SSE Progress

> Project: `ultraplan-go`
> Sprint: `31-web-operations`
> Purpose: the authoritative, human-readable sprint contract. All other sprint artifacts must satisfy these requirements.

## Sprint Goal

Expose existing guarded validation, planning, execute, review, smoke, verify, study run-loop, and cancellation operations through the local web surface with server-issued confirmations and bounded SSE progress, without adding a second workflow engine or durable web-owned state. Gracefully stopping the server must cancel every active server-owned operation through the same product/runtime cleanup paths used by explicit cancellation.

## Required Outputs

| Output | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sprint requirements | `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/31-web-operations/requirements.md` | This sprint contract derived from the project index, roadmap, PRD, TRD, architecture, Sprint 30 artifacts, and prior sprint reviews. |
| Architecture reasoning | `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/31-web-operations/reasoning/architecture.md` | Decision record for operation capabilities, app/web boundaries, mutation locks, cancellation ownership, graceful server draining and cancel-all shutdown, and recovery through durable product state. |
| API design reasoning | `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/31-web-operations/reasoning/api-design.md` | Decision record for confirmation, operation start/status/result/cancellation endpoints, SSE event schema, shutdown-visible operation states, error envelopes, and compatibility constraints. |
| Frontend reasoning | `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/31-web-operations/reasoning/frontend.md` | Decision record for browser confirmations, progress, result, finding, cancellation, server-shutdown interruption, failure, and recovery views using server-rendered pages plus minimal JavaScript. |
| App operation use cases | `../ultraplan-go/internal/app/web_operations.go` | Typed prepare/start/status/cancel operation use cases over existing app operations, with normalized scope, fingerprints, runtime/model summaries, safe progress events, and canonical cancellation propagation. |
| App operation tests | `../ultraplan-go/internal/app/web_operations_test.go` | Covers confirmation binding, supported operation mapping, explicit and server-shutdown cancellation, typed errors, redaction, and CLI/TUI/web agreement with fake dependencies. |
| Sprint mutation lock support | `../ultraplan-go/internal/sprint/locks.go` | Product-owned per-sprint mutation exclusion for sprint flow, execute, review, smoke, and verify operations with actionable conflict diagnostics. |
| Sprint lock tests | `../ultraplan-go/internal/sprint/locks_test.go` | Covers lock acquire/release, conflict reporting, cancellation cleanup, server-shutdown cleanup ordering, stale-lock handling policy, and non-overlap with existing study locks. |
| Web operation hub | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/operations.go` | Bounded ephemeral operation hub with operation IDs, cancellation functions, recent safe event buffers, subscribers, terminal results, short retention, server draining state, and cancel-all shutdown coordination. |
| Web operation routes | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/routes.go` | Adds the confirmed-operation, status/result, SSE, and cancellation routes while preserving Sprint 30 read-only routes and API error behavior. |
| Web operation handlers | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/handlers.go` | Maps HTTP requests to app operation use cases and renders JSON/HTML/SSE without importing product modules or CLI handlers. |
| Web confirmation and CSRF/session support | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/security.go` | Extends local HTTP security with short-lived same-origin mutation protection and confirmation-token validation. |
| Web operation tests | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/operations_test.go` | Covers operation lifecycle, retention, draining, rejection of new work during shutdown, cancellation of all active server-owned operations, bounded cleanup, result projection, conflict handling, redaction, and no durable web state. |
| Web route/API tests | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/routes_test.go` | Covers POST/DELETE methods, prepare/start/status/cancel route shape, API envelopes, method rejection, server-draining responses, and compatibility with Sprint 30 read-only endpoints. |
| SSE tests | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/sse_test.go` | Covers typed SSE events, monotonic event IDs, heartbeat comments, reconnect, buffer rollover, slow subscribers, disconnect behavior, server-shutdown cancellation events, and bounded stream closure. |
| Browser operation templates | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/templates/*.html` | Updates pages/partials for operation scope confirmation, progress, results, findings, failures, cancellation, server shutdown, interruption, and recovery guidance. |
| Browser operation JavaScript | `../ultraplan-go/internal/web/static/*` | Minimal dependency-free progressive enhancement for prepare/start/cancel requests, EventSource subscription, reconnect, and durable-state refresh prompts. |
| Web documentation | `../ultraplan-go/docs/local-web.md` | Documents guarded browser operations, confirmation flow, SSE progress, explicit cancellation, browser disconnect behavior, graceful server shutdown cancellation, recovery, local-only trust limits, and durable state authority. |
| CLI/API documentation updates | `../ultraplan-go/docs/cli-reference.md` | Documents web operation behavior and server shutdown semantics as browser/API affordances over existing CLI/TUI use cases without changing CLI automation semantics. |
| Architecture documentation updates | `../ultraplan-go/docs/architecture.md` | Documents operation-hub ephemerality, server-owned run lifecycle, graceful shutdown draining and cancellation, SSE as progress-only transport, app/product ownership, mutation locks, and no web-owned workflow state. |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/v1/operations/prepare` returns a normalized operation scope, affected workspace/target paths, runtime/model or harness information when relevant, mutation class, current governed-input fingerprint, expiry, and a server-issued confirmation token bound to the normalized request.
- [ ] Mutating or runtime-backed operations cannot start without a valid, unexpired, current confirmation token that matches the normalized start request and current input fingerprint.
- [ ] Supported browser operations are limited to existing app use cases for validation, prompt preview, dry-run, sprint flow, execute, review, smoke, verify, study run-loop, operation status/result inspection, and explicit cancellation.
- [ ] HTTP commands use `POST` for prepare/start and `DELETE` for cancellation; SSE is one-way progress only and cannot start, mutate, complete, fail, or cancel work.
- [ ] The operation hub is bounded and ephemeral: it stores only safe recent events, subscribers, cancellation handles, and terminal results for short retention, and server restart recovery rereads durable product state.
- [ ] Every operation started by the server is owned by the server lifecycle, including its root context, cancellation function, nested tasks, runtime or harness calls, process tree, locks, progress publication, cleanup, and durable terminal-state reconciliation; detached background runs that intentionally outlive the server are not supported.
- [ ] SSE emits typed event names with monotonic event IDs, heartbeat comments, safe redacted payloads, and reconnect behavior that resumes from buffered events when available or instructs the browser to refresh durable status when not.
- [ ] A disconnected or slow browser subscriber cannot block the underlying app operation, cannot change the operation result, and cancels only its own subscription.
- [ ] Explicit cancellation reaches the shared app operation context, product/runtime cleanup path, or smoke-harness cleanup path as applicable, and leaves durable state recoverable from CLI, TUI, and browser status views.
- [ ] Graceful server shutdown enters a draining state, rejects new operation starts, prevents queued work from beginning, records `reason: server_shutdown`, invokes every active operation's canonical cancellation function exactly once, propagates cancellation through nested tasks and owned process trees, waits for bounded cleanup and reconciliation, persists a truthful cancelled, interrupted, or cleanup-uncertain outcome, and only then closes SSE streams and exits.
- [ ] A graceful shutdown deadline that expires must escalate cleanup for remaining owned process trees and record interruption or cleanup uncertainty; it must not report success, release mutation locks as though cleanup succeeded, or leave active child processes intentionally detached.
- [ ] After a crash or forced termination, the next server start reconciles stale running operations and locks from durable product state, marks unresolved work interrupted or recovery-required, and never promotes stale running state to success.
- [ ] Conflicting sprint mutations and existing study run-loop mutations fail with actionable conflict diagnostics rather than running concurrently; sprint mutation exclusion is owned by `internal/sprint`, not by HTTP middleware alone.
- [ ] Structured API errors cover conflict, stale confirmation, invalid request, validation failure, runtime failure, cancellation, server draining, unavailable prerequisite, timeout, and internal failure without leaking secrets, raw provider payloads, unrestricted stderr, or absolute local paths.
- [ ] Browser pages show operation scope before confirmation and show truthful progress, final result, findings, failures, explicit or server-shutdown cancellation status, stale/reconnect guidance, and recovery actions after completion or interruption.
- [ ] `internal/web` does not import `internal/study`, `internal/project`, `internal/sprint`, runtime adapters, process adapters, or CLI handlers; HTTP handlers call typed `internal/app` use cases only.
- [ ] Existing CLI and TUI behavior remain supported and unchanged except for shared app-use-case additions required by the web surface.
- [ ] Normal verification passes with deterministic fakes: focused app operation tests, focused sprint lock tests, focused web operation/SSE/security/route/template tests, graceful-shutdown cancel-all and restart-reconciliation tests, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `go build ./cmd/ultraplan` from `../ultraplan-go`.

## Non-Goals

- Adding new product workflows, new sprint stages, or a browser-specific workflow engine is not included.
- Detached or daemonized local operations that intentionally survive graceful server shutdown are not included; a future durable worker architecture must define separate leases, heartbeats, ownership, and reconciliation before survival across control-plane restart is allowed.
- Browser editing of arbitrary workspace files, generated artifacts, project docs, plans, review findings, or smoke issue records is not included.
- Hosted SaaS, LAN/public binding, remote access, accounts, authentication teams, permissions, tenants, collaboration, remote workers, and remote workspace synchronization are not included.
- WebSockets, bidirectional terminal/session transport, live agent chat, or browser-driven remote shell/process control is not included.
- A database-backed state model, browser-owned durable state, durable web job queue, or operation history replacing product run state is not included.
- New review, smoke, execute, planning, or study run-loop semantics are not included; the browser may only expose current app use cases.
- General-purpose issue tracking, issue assignment, project-management features, automatic product fixes, and automatic Git mutation are not included.
- A frontend framework, Node.js runtime, Vite, separate frontend process, service worker, or asset build pipeline is not included.
- Browser-level API compatibility hardening, accessibility release audit, gated real-runtime browser evidence, and release packaging are deferred to Sprint 32 unless needed to prove Sprint 31 behavior with fakes.

## Constraints

- `internal/web` may depend on `internal/app` operation/query interfaces and plain result types only; it must not import product modules, runtime/process adapters, or CLI command handlers directly.
- HTTP handlers must not invoke `ultraplan` as a subprocess, parse CLI output, duplicate product validators, duplicate workflow state machines, or decide review/smoke/execute verdicts.
- The server operation hub is transport-lifecycle state only; workspace artifacts, `flow-state.json`, `.run-state.json`, study run state, `review.md`, `smoke.md`, and external harness evidence remain authoritative.
- Confirmation tokens must be short-lived, same-server-issued, bound to normalized operation scope and current fingerprints, and invalidated by stale inputs or mismatched requests.
- Product-owned locks must guard mutations; HTTP middleware may enforce request policy but must not be the only concurrency guard.
- SSE buffers, active operations, subscribers, request bodies, event payloads, and retention windows must be explicitly bounded.
- Browser disconnect cancels only the SSE subscription; explicit cancellation must use the operation cancellation endpoint and shared app context.
- Graceful server shutdown is different from browser disconnect: it must stop accepting new mutations, cancel every active server-owned operation, use the canonical cancellation and cleanup path, and wait for bounded terminal-state reconciliation before process exit.
- Mutation locks and cleanup ownership must remain held until the affected operation has reached a truthful terminal or cleanup-uncertain state; shutdown must not release them early merely to complete HTTP server closure.
- The Phase 4 server remains loopback-only, same-origin, CSRF-protected, body-limited, timeout-bounded, Host/Origin-validated, security-header-protected, and redaction-safe.
- The UI must remain Go `html/template` plus embedded CSS/minimal dependency-free JavaScript; no frontend build step or browser-owned product state is allowed.
- Tests must use `httptest`, fake app use cases, fake runtimes, fake smoke harnesses, and deterministic temporary workspaces by default; real runtime/harness/browser tests are gated or deferred.
- Automatic Git add, commit, push, branch, merge, reset, or other Git mutation remains prohibited.

## Dependencies

| Prior Sprint / Output | Required For | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sprint 30: `projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/30-web-foundations/requirements.md` and implementation outputs | Local web foundation | Sprint 31 builds on `ultraplan serve`, loopback security, `/api/v1` envelopes, embedded templates/static assets, artifact previews, and explicit `cmd -> app+tui+web` composition. |
| Sprint 30 query-only app/web boundary | Operation boundary design | Mutation-capable app operation use cases must be separate from the read-only facade rather than broadening web capability accidentally. |
| Sprints 24-25 TUI operational controls | Guarded local operation precedent | Browser operations must match the existing confirmation/progress/cancellation discipline exposed by TUI use cases. |
| Sprints 26-29 review, smoke, and verify use cases | Browser verification operations | Web review, smoke, verify, findings, and recovery views must call existing app use cases and preserve review-before-smoke, verdict, staleness, and harness-evidence semantics. |
| Sprint 23 execute use cases and `.run-state.json` | Browser execute operation/status | Web execute operations must preserve durable task state, deterministic task IDs, cancellation, diagnostics, and no Git mutation. |
| Study run-loop locking and cancellation behavior | Browser study run-loop operation | Web study operations must use existing study locks and durable state rather than adding HTTP-owned study scheduling. |
| `../ultraplan-go/docs/plans/server-shutdown-run-cancellation-contract.md` | Graceful shutdown ownership and cancellation | Defines the normative draining, cancel-all, process-tree cleanup, terminal-state, SSE closure, forced-termination reconciliation, and future durable-worker boundaries that Sprint 31 must implement. |
| `projects/ultraplan-go/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` Phase 4 rules | Package layout and dependency direction | Defines `internal/web` ownership, operation hub ephemerality, and prohibition on web-owned workflow state. |
| `projects/ultraplan-go/docs/TRD.md` sections 7.5 and 18A | HTTP, SSE, operation, security, and testing scope | Sprint 31 implements guarded operations and SSE progress subset of Phase 4. |
| `projects/ultraplan-go/docs/PRD.md` browser operation scenario | Product behavior and non-goals | Confirms browser operations are local, guarded, and backed by durable workspace state. |

## Review Expectations

| What | How Verified |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmation preflight is binding and current | Run focused app/web confirmation tests and inspect fingerprint, normalized-scope, expiry, token-binding, and stale-input checks. |
| Operation endpoints are method-correct and scoped | Run route/API tests for prepare, start, status/result, SSE, cancellation, method rejection, server-draining rejection, and unknown `/api/` behavior. |
| SSE is progress-only and bounded | Run SSE tests for event IDs, event names, heartbeat, reconnect, buffer rollover, slow subscribers, disconnect, server-shutdown cancellation events, bounded closure, and absence of command semantics. |
| Explicit cancellation reaches product work | Run app/web cancellation tests with fake runtime and fake harness operations; inspect durable-state recovery assertions. |
| Graceful shutdown cancels all server-owned work | Start multiple fake long-running operations, initiate graceful shutdown, verify draining and rejection of new starts, verify each canonical cancel function is called once, verify nested runtime/harness/process cleanup and bounded wait, assert truthful durable terminal or interrupted state, confirm locks are released only after reconciliation, and confirm the server and SSE streams then close. |
| Crash and forced-stop recovery is truthful | Seed stale running state and locks, restart the server, and verify reconciliation reports interrupted or recovery-required rather than success. |
| Product mutation locks prevent conflicts | Run sprint lock and study-operation conflict tests; inspect diagnostics for actionable scope/lock information. |
| Web boundary remains transport-only | Inspect `internal/web` imports and handlers; confirm no direct product/runtime/process/CLI-handler dependencies. |
| Durable state remains authoritative | Review operation hub implementation and tests proving restart/refresh reads product state and no durable web job store is introduced. |
| Browser UI is truthful and progressively enhanced | Run template/static tests and inspect views for scope confirmation, progress, result, findings, failure, explicit cancellation, server-shutdown interruption, reconnect, and recovery states. |
| Security and redaction remain enforced | Run Host/Origin/CSRF/body-limit/security-header/redaction tests covering mutating routes and SSE responses. |
| Existing surfaces do not regress | Run focused app dispatch/TUI/CLI agreement tests and full `go test ./...`. |
| Sprint verification passes | Run `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `go build ./cmd/ultraplan` from `../ultraplan-go`. |

# Sprint 35 Requirements: Durable Run Identity and Cross-Surface Observability

> Project: `ultraplan-go`
> Sprint: `35-durable-run-observability`
> Purpose: the authoritative, human-readable sprint contract. Later sprint artifacts must reason through the open decisions and satisfy the fixed observable outcomes.

## Sprint Goal

Make every accepted runtime-backed UltraPlan execution a durable, workspace-visible run that can be discovered, inspected, followed, cancelled when authorized, and reconciled consistently from CLI, TUI, and any local web-server instance attached to the same workspace.

The sprint repairs the operational control plane exposed by real use: CLI-started work must appear in the browser running-process indicator, a run opened through another server must retain useful history and continue with live events, and a browser session or server restart must not turn a legitimate run into an unexplained `404 Operation not retained` dead end.

This sprint does not change the authority of project, sprint, study, or Markdown artifacts. Durable operational run state is a separate product concern from the later gated decision about alternate persistence for authored product content.

## Required Outputs

| Deliverable | Required Outcome |
|---|---|
| Run identity and lifecycle model | A stable workspace-scoped run ID, attempt identity, operation/stage identity, timestamps, ownership/liveness facts, safe correlation fields, and one arbitrated terminal outcome exist independently of a browser session, HTTP server process, or event subscriber. |
| Durable run repository and event journal | Accepted runs and sanitized progress events are durably recorded before they are advertised as observable; events have monotonic per-run ordering and can be replayed after reconnect, session expiry, or server restart. The reasoning and plan stages select the concrete package and storage mechanism. |
| Workspace-wide active-run projection | CLI, TUI, dashboard, project, sprint, study, and local web surfaces derive running counts and run lists from the same workspace-wide lifecycle model rather than the current web process's in-memory operation map or only the page currently being viewed. |
| Stable run inspection | A durable run detail surface reports identity, target, lifecycle state, latest heartbeat, stage/task progress, safe diagnostics, event history, terminal result, and recovery guidance. Read visibility is not coupled to the browser session that started the work. |
| Replayable live event delivery | The web event transport resumes from a durable sequence cursor, makes truncation or retention gaps explicit, and continues from durable state when a different local server instance serves the same workspace. SSE may remain the transport; the transport is not the source of truth. |
| Ownership, lease, and reconciliation | Active executions publish enough owner/lease/heartbeat and process/runtime identity to distinguish live, stalled, interrupted, cleanup-uncertain, and terminal work conservatively, including PID reuse and abrupt owner death. Startup and periodic reconciliation never infer success from process absence or artifact presence. |
| Cross-surface cancellation | Authorized cancellation resolves the durable run, reaches the current owner through a selected coordination mechanism, is idempotent, and participates in the same single-terminal-outcome arbitration as completion, failure, timeout, interruption, and server shutdown. |
| Compatibility and migration | Current sprint/study locks, flow state, execute state, runtime checkpoints, operation URLs, and JSON clients have an explicit migration or compatibility story. Legacy or expired operation links resolve to a durable run, a retained tombstone, or precise recovery guidance rather than a generic dashboard error. |
| Operational telemetry | Structured logs, local metrics, diagnostics, and optional traces share run/attempt/stage/task/runtime correlation. Operator-visible health distinguishes storage failure, stale ownership, reconciliation backlog, replay gap, subscriber lag/drop, and cancellation uncertainty. |
| Verification and fault injection | Deterministic, race, integration, and browser tests prove CLI-to-web discovery, multiple local servers, refresh/reconnect replay, session expiry, server restart, abrupt owner death, stale leases, PID reuse, slow subscribers, bounded storage, duplicate cancellation, and terminal-state races. |
| Documentation | Architecture, PRD, TRD, CLI/API, local-web, operations, and recovery documentation explain the lifecycle model, authority boundaries, visibility guarantees, retention behavior, diagnostic workflow, compatibility policy, and intentionally unresolved design choices. |

## Acceptance Criteria

- A runtime-backed command receives a durable run ID before child execution begins, or fails closed without starting the child when required run persistence cannot be established.
- Two concurrent CLI-started runs in one workspace appear as two active runs in the browser top bar and workspace run list without requiring navigation to either owning sprint or study page.
- Work started through CLI, TUI, or one local web-server instance can be inspected from another supported local surface attached to the same workspace.
- Opening a current run through a different local server provides retained event history and subsequently committed live events, subject only to an explicit documented topology boundary selected during reasoning.
- Refreshing a page, rotating or expiring a browser session, restarting the observing server, or losing an SSE connection does not erase the run identity or turn a valid run into an unexplained 404.
- Every event visible to a subscriber has a stable run ID and monotonic per-run sequence. Reconnect resumes from a cursor; if the requested history is unavailable, the API emits a typed gap/retention response and a current durable snapshot.
- Running counts use lifecycle state from the shared run projection. No UI depends on a planning-stage status value that cannot represent running execution.
- Active-run truth includes a renewable lease or equivalent liveness contract. Reconciliation is conservative, observable, idempotent, and safe against stale PIDs and owner crashes.
- Exactly one terminal outcome wins for completion, failure, cancellation, timeout, interruption, cleanup uncertainty, and reconciliation races. Repeated observers and cancellation requests cannot rewrite that outcome inconsistently.

# Server Shutdown and Active Run Cancellation Contract

**Status:** Proposed, normative addendum  
**Applies to:** `docs/plans/integrated-roadmap.md` and `docs/plans/ultraplan-local-server-experiment-plan.md`  
**Scope:** Filesystem-backed local server and all later server-backed UltraPlan modes

## 1. Core rule

> Gracefully stopping the UltraPlan server cancels every active run owned by that server.

The initial local server must not leave agent processes, study run loops, sprint flows, verification attempts, repairs, shell commands, or other server-started operations running after the server that owns their lifecycle, locks, progress streams, and cancellation controls has stopped.

This rule applies whether shutdown begins through:

- a browser or administrative stop action;
- `SIGINT`;
- `SIGTERM`;
- normal process shutdown initiated by the application.

A browser tab closing, navigating away, losing its SSE connection, or temporarily disconnecting does **not** cancel a run. Runs are owned by the server operation lifecycle, not by an individual HTTP request or browser connection.

1: # Server Shutdown and Active Run Cancellation Contract
2: 
3: **Status:** Proposed, normative addendum  
4: **Applies to:** `docs/plans/integrated-roadmap.md` and `docs/plans/ultraplan-local-server-experiment-plan.md`  
5: **Scope:** Filesystem-backed local server and all later server-backed UltraPlan modes
6: 
7: ## 1. Core rule
8: 
9: > Gracefully stopping the UltraPlan server cancels every active run owned by that server.
10: 
11: The initial local server must not leave agent processes, study run loops, sprint flows, verification attempts, repairs, shell commands, or other server-started operations running after the server that owns their lifecycle, locks, progress streams, and cancellation controls has stopped.
12: 
13: This rule applies whether shutdown begins through:
14: 
15: - a browser or administrative stop action;
16: - `SIGINT`;
17: - `SIGTERM`;
18: - normal process shutdown initiated by the application.
19: 
20: A browser tab closing, navigating away, losing its SSE connection, or temporarily disconnecting does **not** cancel a run. Runs are owned by the server operation lifecycle, not by an individual HTTP request or browser connection.
21: 
22: ## 2. Ownership boundary
23: 
24: For the filesystem-backed local product, an operation started through CLI, TUI, or HTTP is owned by the process executing that operation.
25: 
26: A server-owned operation includes:
27: 
28: - its root `context.Context` and cancellation function;
29: - runtime and provider calls;
30: - child processes and process groups;
31: - retries and rate-limit waits;
32: - task or shard workers;
33: - scope locks and leases;
34: - progress publication;
35: - durable attempt and stage state;
36: - cleanup and reconciliation responsibility.
37: 
38: The initial server does not support detached background execution that intentionally survives server termination.
39: 
40: A future durable worker architecture may change ownership so runs survive control-plane restart, but that must be introduced as an explicit later contract with durable workers, leases, heartbeats, and reconciliation. It must not emerge accidentally from orphaned local processes.
41: 
42: ## 3. Graceful shutdown sequence
43: 
44: When graceful shutdown begins, the server must perform this sequence:
45: 
46: ```text
47: running
48:   -> draining
49:   -> cancellation requested for all active server-owned operations
50:   -> bounded cleanup and reconciliation
51:   -> durable terminal or interrupted state
52:   -> HTTP/SSE shutdown
53:   -> process exit
54: ```
55: 
56: ### 3.1 Enter draining state
57: 
58: The server must first:
59: 
60: - mark itself as draining;
61: - stop accepting new mutating operations;
62: - reject new run starts with a stable `server_draining` or equivalent error;
63: - prevent queued work that has not begun from starting;
64: - allow only the bounded reads needed to display shutdown progress where practical.
65: 
66: ### 3.2 Request cancellation
67: 
68: For every active operation, the server must:
69: 
70: - persist or publish `cancellation_requested` where durable operation state exists;
71: - record `reason: server_shutdown`;
72: - record the request timestamp;
73: - invoke the operation's canonical cancellation function exactly once;
74: - propagate cancellation to nested tasks, runtime adapters, waits, and subprocess execution.
75: 
76: Server shutdown must use the same cancellation and cleanup path as an explicit user cancellation. It must not invent a weaker process-only termination path.
77: 
78: ### 3.3 Stop runtime and process trees
79: 
80: Cancellation must reach the runtime boundary and terminate the complete owned process tree according to the existing AgentWrap and runtime cleanup guarantees.
81: 
82: The server must not consider an operation stopped merely because:
83: 
84: - the top-level goroutine returned;
85: - the immediate child process exited;
86: - the SSE client disconnected;
87: - the provider call stopped producing events.
88: 
89: Owned descendants, pipes, temporary resources, locks, and workspaces must be reconciled or reported as uncertain.
90: 
91: ### 3.4 Wait for bounded cleanup
92: 
93: The server must wait for a configured, bounded shutdown grace period.
94: 
95: During that period it should:
96: 
97: - continue collecting terminal runtime events;
98: - allow operation state to reach a durable terminal result;
99: - wait for process-tree cleanup;
100: - persist final diagnostics and artifacts that can be captured safely;
101: - release locks only after the owning operation has stopped or reconciliation has established that it no longer owns live work.
102: 
103: The server must never wait indefinitely.
104: 
105: ### 3.5 Persist the correct outcome
106: 
107: After cancellation and cleanup, each operation must end as one of:
108: 
109: - `cancelled`: cancellation was accepted and owned work was stopped cleanly;
110: - `interrupted`: shutdown prevented normal completion and the full final outcome could not be established;
111: - `cleanup_uncertain`: cancellation was requested, but descendant-process, workspace, lock, or resource cleanup could not be proven;
112: - `failed`: a separate failure was already authoritative before shutdown cancellation took effect.
113: 
114: Where the state model supports structured reasons, preserve:
115: 
116: ```text
117: terminal_status: cancelled
118: cancellation_reason: server_shutdown
119: ```
120: 
121: Do not represent shutdown cancellation as:
122: 
123: - successful completion;
124: - ordinary user cancellation without the shutdown reason;
125: - a missing or silently abandoned run;
126: - a completed stage merely because an artifact happens to exist.
127: 
128: Artifact validation and canonical stage rules remain authoritative after cancellation.
129: 
130: ### 3.6 Finish progress streams and stop HTTP
131: 
132: Where possible, publish a final bounded event for each affected operation, such as:
133: 
134: ```text
135: operation_cancelled reason=server_shutdown
136: operation_interrupted reason=server_shutdown
137: cleanup_uncertain reason=server_shutdown
138: ```
139: 
140: Then:
141: 
142: - close operation event subscriptions;
143: - close SSE responses;
144: - gracefully stop the HTTP server;
145: - exit after all operations have reached a durable outcome or the grace period has expired and uncertainty has been recorded.
146: 
147: ## 4. Browser and administrative UX
148: 
149: ### 4.1 Stopping from the browser
150: 
151: If a browser-accessible stop-server action is introduced and active runs exist, the UI must show a confirmation that states:
152: 
153: - how many operations are active;
154: - their kinds and scopes;
155: - that stopping the server will cancel them;
156: - that partial work will be preserved only where current recovery guarantees allow;
157: - that cleanup uncertainty may require reconciliation on restart.
158: 
159: After confirmation, shutdown proceeds without requiring separate cancellation confirmation for each run.
160: 
161: If no runs are active, the server may stop without the additional active-run warning.
162: 
163: ### 4.2 Signals and non-interactive shutdown
164: 
165: `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` cannot depend on an interactive confirmation. They must begin the graceful shutdown sequence immediately.
166: 
167: A second termination signal may shorten the remaining grace period, but it should still attempt final state persistence before forced exit where possible.
168: 
169: ### 4.3 Browser disconnection
170: 
171: The following must not cancel a run:
172: 
173: - closing the browser tab;
174: - refreshing the page;
175: - losing network connectivity;
176: - an SSE timeout;
177: - reconnecting from another browser session.
178: 
179: The user must be able to reconnect and observe the current durable operation state while the server remains alive.
180: 
181: ## 5. Forced termination and crash recovery
182: 
183: `SIGKILL`, host failure, power loss, runtime crash, or an unrecoverable server panic cannot guarantee graceful cancellation.
184: 
185: On the next startup, UltraPlan must reconcile any operation recorded as active but lacking a valid live owner.
186: 
187: Reconciliation should:
188: 
189: 1. inspect durable operation, attempt, lock, and runtime state;
190: 2. determine whether an owned process is still alive where this can be checked safely;
191: 3. terminate or quarantine confirmed leftover owned processes where supported;
192: 4. preserve valid partial artifacts and diagnostics without promoting them to canonical success;
193: 5. mark the operation `interrupted` or `cleanup_uncertain`;
194: 6. clear or repair stale locks only after ownership has been checked;
195: 7. expose a recovery recommendation in CLI, TUI, and browser status.
196: 
197: A stale `running` record must never remain indefinitely, and restart reconciliation must never infer success merely from process absence.
198: 
199: ## 6. Concurrency and state rules
200: 
201: - Shutdown cancellation is idempotent.
202: - Each active operation has one authoritative cancellation owner.
203: - New operations are rejected after draining begins.
204: - An operation completing concurrently with shutdown uses the existing terminal-outcome arbitration rules; shutdown cancellation must not overwrite an already committed authoritative completion, and late completion must not overwrite an accepted cancellation.
205: - Lock release follows terminal ownership and cleanup, not HTTP request lifetime.
206: - The server process must not exit while it still claims active operations without first recording interruption or cleanup uncertainty.
207: - `flow-state.json` and other summary state must not become a detailed shutdown database; they should retain canonical outcome, freshness, reason, and pointers to detailed attempt evidence.
208: 
209: ## 7. Configuration
210: 
211: The server may expose a bounded shutdown grace period, for example:
212: 
213: ```yaml
214: server:
215:   shutdown_grace_period: 30s
216: ```
217: 
218: Requirements:
219: 
220: - provide a safe default;
221: - reject invalid or unbounded values;
222: - include the effective value in diagnostics;
223: - do not allow configuration to disable cancellation of server-owned runs;
224: - distinguish the HTTP shutdown timeout from operation cleanup budgets if they need different values.
225: 
226: ## 8. Required observability
227: 
228: The browser, CLI, logs, and structured events should make shutdown behavior visible through fields such as:
229: 
230: ```text
231: server_state
232: drain_started_at
233: active_operation_count
234: operation_id
235: operation_kind
236: scope
237: cancellation_requested_at
238: cancellation_reason
239: cleanup_status
240: terminal_status
241: recovery_required
242: ```
243: 
244: Secrets, full prompts, unsafe environment values, and unbounded provider payloads remain excluded.
245: 
246: ## 9. Required tests
247: 
248: ### 9.1 Graceful shutdown
249: 
250: Cover:
251: 
252: - stopping an idle server;
253: - `SIGINT` with one active run;
254: - `SIGTERM` with several active operations;
255: - cancellation propagation to nested runtime work;
256: - process-tree cleanup;
257: - bounded grace-period expiry;
258: - final state persistence before exit;
259: - final SSE event and stream closure;
260: - lock release after confirmed cleanup;
261: - rejection of new operations while draining.
262: 
263: ### 9.2 Terminal races
264: 
265: Cover:
266: 
267: - operation completes immediately before shutdown cancellation;
268: - cancellation is accepted before a late successful completion publishes;
269: - failure becomes authoritative while shutdown is beginning;
270: - repeated shutdown or cancellation requests;
271: - second termination signal during cleanup.
272: 
273: Exactly one authoritative terminal outcome must be committed.
274: 
275: ### 9.3 Browser behavior
276: 
277: Cover:
278: 
279: - closing a tab does not cancel a run;
280: - SSE disconnect does not cancel a run;
281: - reconnect shows current state;
282: - stop-server confirmation lists active operations;
283: - confirmed browser shutdown cancels all active runs.
284: 
285: ### 9.4 Crash and restart
286: 
287: Cover:
288: 
289: - process death before final state write;
290: - stale active-operation records;
291: - stale locks;
292: - leftover child processes where the platform permits testing;
293: - valid partial artifacts after interruption;
294: - startup reconciliation producing `interrupted` or `cleanup_uncertain`, never success.
295: 
296: ### 9.5 Parity
297: 
298: The same underlying cancellation, cleanup, terminal arbitration, and recovery behavior must be exercised whether the operation was started from CLI, TUI, or HTTP.
299: 
300: ## 10. Exit criteria for the web foundation
301: 
302: The web foundation is not complete until:
303: 
304: - graceful server shutdown cancels every active server-owned run;
305: - cancellation reaches runtime and owned process trees;
306: - shutdown waits for bounded cleanup;
307: - each affected operation receives a durable, truthful outcome;
308: - browser disconnection is independent from run cancellation;
309: - restart reconciles abruptly interrupted work;
310: - active-run shutdown behavior is visible and tested;
311: - no orphaned local execution is treated as supported detached work.
312: 
313: ## 11. Final decision
314: 
315: For the initial filesystem-backed server:
316: 
317: ```text
318: browser disconnect -> run continues
319: explicit run cancellation -> that run is cancelled
320: server graceful shutdown -> all server-owned active runs are cancelled
321: server crash or forced kill -> next startup reconciles them as interrupted or cleanup-uncertain
322: ```
323: 
324: This contract remains in force until UltraPlan deliberately introduces a durable execution service whose workers, leases, and ownership semantics allow runs to survive control-plane restart.

(End of file - total 324 lines)
</content>
